title: Points of Judgement at the Agronomy Desk: Days of Grace on a Freshly Reviewed Crop Input Purchasing Account
content:
Questions the agronomy desk is answered on where a member of the Crop Input Purchasing Accounts asks how long they have before a service charge bites, and their account has been reviewed lately.

**The account was reviewed recently and credit approved it. How many days of grace does it carry?** Where the account's most recent credit review was completed inside the programme's review interval, counted in whole months from the day the review completed to the handling date, and the credit department's standing decision on the account is an approval, the days of grace are 30.

**And where the standing decision is conditional rather than an approval?** Where the account's most recent credit review was completed inside that interval, counted the same way, and that decision is conditional, the days of grace are 20.

**The last review is older than the programme's interval. What then?** In that case no substituted days of grace apply on the Crop Input Purchasing Accounts, whatever the standing decision.

**What counts as inside the interval?** The interval is the programme's own, counted in whole months from the day the review completed to the handling date. The intervals stand as follows: 0 months on the Cash Purchase Account and the Early Pay Prepay Program Account, which are not reviewed at all; 24 months on the Standard 30-Day Charge Account; and 12 months on the Seasonal Terms Crop Input Account, the Full Acre Input Financing Account and the Precision Partner Input Program Account. A review completed 11 months before the handling date on a programme whose interval is 12 months is inside it; a review completed 13 months before it is not.

**Is the member's word on the review enough?** The review the days of grace are read from is the review standing on the account, and the decision is the decision standing on the account.
